To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cry1Ab gene from B. thuringensisis an effective tool for managing stem borer and foliage feeding pests in aromatic rice and that resistance to the B. thuringien-sis toxin is not likely to develop in the near future.

the resistance of an aromatic rice variety transformed with a B. thuringiensi cry1Ab gene to lepidopteran stem borers and foliage feeders was influenced by the age of the plant, the age of the larvae, and the application of fertilizer.

the resistance of vegetative stage plants of a cry1Ac-transformed aromatic rice to four lepidopteron pests was greater than that of control plants, but resistance was not as great in flowering stage plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of transgenic rice with enhanced resistance to insect pests.
the effect of plant age, plant growth stage, and fertilizer treatment on resistance of a cry1 Ab- transformed aromatic rice to lepidopteran stem borers and foliage feeders.
the development of insect-resistant transgenic rice varieties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cry1Ab gene in the transgenic line of rice tested is a valuable tool for resistance to the stem borers and leaf folder, but the level of resistance is not adequate to control the leaf folder.
the transgenic rice variety 827 is resistant to C. suppressalis and C. medinals at the vegetative growth stage and is resistant to Cnaphaloccrocis at the vegetative and flowering growth stages.
the cry1Ab gene is not a good candidate for resistance management in this rice variety.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a Bt rice line can be resistant to a variety of rice insect pests, but the level of resistance can vary depending on the plant age and the insect species.
a B. thuringens toxin gene, such as the cry1Ab gene, can be used to control stem borers in vegetative stage plants but not flowering plants.
the resistance of the cry1ab transgenic rice line 827 to stem borers was variable, depending on the species, age of plant, age of larva, and fertilizer treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the resistance of the cry1A gene is not stable over time.
resistance management is not necessary for the use of Bt rice, as the Bt trait is stable and the rice plant does not develop resistance to Bt.
the resistance of the transformed rice line to lepidopteran stem borers and foliage feeders was affected by plant age, larval age, and fertilizer treatment.
